item.title: Chlorophyll extremes during a surface marine heatwave in a seasonally stratified shelf sea
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04118-2

A strong 2023 marine heatwave enhanced surface chlorophyll, with particularly persistent increases below the surface in the Firth of Forth, Scotland, according to high-resolution in situ observations.
item.dc:title: Chlorophyll extremes during a surface marine heatwave in a seasonally stratified shelf sea

item.title: Satellite altimetry reveals heterogeneity in global flood peak timing and its shifts
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04115-5

Flood peak timing shifted earlier at 52.2% of river virtual stations and 27 of the 50 largest basin outlets, especially at high latitudes and elevations, according to a study using satellite altimetry and clustering analysis to investigate global flood peak timing and its trends from 2008 to 2025.
item.dc:title: Satellite altimetry reveals heterogeneity in global flood peak timing and its shifts

item.title: Fire-derived ozone intensifies carbon loss in Amazon forests under extreme droughts
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04047-0

Fire-derived ozone increases carbon losses from the Amazon by about one quarter of direct fire emissions, with damage persisting during extreme drought despite stomatal limitation, based on land-surface modelling of fire activity, ozone exposure, and climate variability.
item.dc:title: Fire-derived ozone intensifies carbon loss in Amazon forests under extreme droughts

item.title: Fluid inclusions establish natron as a key astrobiological target on Enceladus
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04080-z

Natron precipitation traps and preserves pockets of parent fluid, providing a window into the geochemistry of Saturn’s moon Enceladus’ interior, establishing it as a mineral of high astrobiological importance, shown using freezing behaviour experiments and combined synchrotron X-ray computed microtomography and diffraction.
item.dc:title: Fluid inclusions establish natron as a key astrobiological target on Enceladus

item.title: Carbon source and pollutant matching shapes microbial succession and removal regimes under electrochemical redox control
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04100-y

Decision-oriented carbon supplementation in electro-assisted and related anaerobic wastewater treatment systems reshapes niches and interspecies dependencies, leading to around 4-fold increase in pollutant removal, based on experiments pairing three carbon sources with three pollutants.
item.dc:title: Carbon source and pollutant matching shapes microbial succession and removal regimes under electrochemical redox control

item.title: Marine arsenate evolution during Proterozoic oxygenation events and implications for biological phosphate metabolism
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03976-0

Arsenate-to-phosphate ratios increased with the Great Oxygenation Event, potentially limiting productivity and oxygenation. Post-glaciation phosphorus enrichment during the Neoproterozoic Oxygenation Event reduced ratios toward modern levels, enhancing phosphate metabolism, oxygenation, marine productivity and supporting eukaryotic expansion.
item.dc:title: Marine arsenate evolution during Proterozoic oxygenation events and implications for biological phosphate metabolism

item.title: Cascading fishery collapse associated with thermal habitat degradation, marine heatwaves, and predator influx
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04110-w

Early-summer La Niña conditions amplify marine heatwaves that are contributing to the collapse of the Japanese flying squid fishery and increasing the risk of a zero-catch state by the 2040 s, according to multi-decadal observations and climate projections.
item.dc:title: Cascading fishery collapse associated with thermal habitat degradation, marine heatwaves, and predator influx

item.title: Herbaceous leaf hydraulic trade-offs shape ecosystem function across the Mongolian Plateau
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04121-7

A community-wide trade-off between hydraulic efficiency and safety shapes dryland ecosystem function, with efficiency promoting biomass but safety improving water-use efficiency and stability, based on hydraulic trait surveys across 306 sites along a Mongolian Plateau precipitation gradient.
item.dc:title: Herbaceous leaf hydraulic trade-offs shape ecosystem function across the Mongolian Plateau
